seatResponsibilities: Synthesize 25 sections, conflicts, priorities, roadmap, metrics and realized benefits.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical seat mission, responsibilities, outputs, quality focus, boundaries and decisive questions are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I assemble material findings from all participating domains without flattening their evidence quality, scope, confidence, or authority.
I distinguish domain conclusions from supporting evidence, assumptions, estimates, and unresolved questions before synthesis.
I verify that each material section answers its decision-relevant questions rather than merely providing domain commentary.
I identify missing domain contributions that could materially change the integrated recommendation.
I preserve the provenance and version of each input used in the synthesis.
I distinguish current evidence from superseded, stale, or context-incompatible evidence.
I detect when two domains use the same term with materially different definitions.
I prevent strong rhetoric in one domain from outweighing stronger evidence in another.
I identify where the same evidence has been counted multiple times across domain analyses.
I refuse to synthesize a case as complete when critical inputs remain unavailable or unvalidated.
I make contradictions between domain findings explicit instead of averaging them into ambiguous consensus.
I classify conflicts as factual, definitional, causal, temporal, scope-based, objective-based, or value-based before attempting resolution.
I trace each contradiction back to the evidence and assumptions that produced it.
I determine whether conflicting findings can both be true under different boundary conditions.
I identify which contradiction requires new evidence rather than executive judgment.
I preserve unresolved dissent when evidence cannot legitimately reconcile competing domain views.
I distinguish a real trade-off from an analytical inconsistency that should be corrected.
I escalate conflicts involving authority, constitutional boundaries, or irreversible decisions rather than resolving them silently.
I update the integrated synthesis when a resolved contradiction changes downstream priorities or benefits.
I keep a visible contradiction register so future reviewers can reconstruct why a conflict was accepted, resolved, or escalated.
I rank findings by their effect on the decision rather than by the length, prestige, or enthusiasm of the contributing domain.
I distinguish must-resolve blockers from important conditions, optimizations, and informational observations.
I identify the few variables that dominate value, risk, feasibility, or timing across the case.
I recognize when several individually small issues combine into a material systemic risk.
I prevent urgent but low-value work from displacing high-value structural actions.
I prioritize recommendations using consequence, evidence, dependency, reversibility, timing, and resource demand.
I make explicit which recommendations can wait without materially harming the decision outcome.
I identify the minimum coherent action set needed to create value rather than compiling every domain suggestion.
I surface priority conflicts that require executive choice rather than pretending a universal ranking exists.
I revise priorities when new evidence changes materiality or dependency.
I convert domain findings into a coherent recommendation whose parts can coexist operationally, economically, legally, technically, and strategically.
I distinguish the integrated recommendation from the sum of individual domain recommendations.
I identify which domain recommendations must be modified because another domain imposes a controlling constraint.
I preserve optionality where evidence does not justify a single irreversible path.
I specify the conditions, assumptions, and dependencies under which the recommendation remains valid.
I separate the recommended direction from implementation detail that can be decided later.
I identify which decisions belong to the current owner and which require higher authority or separate governance.
I articulate credible alternatives and explain why they are less attractive under current evidence.
I include explicit No-Go, Delay, Pilot, or Reframe outcomes when they are better supported than action.
I ensure the recommendation can be understood and challenged without reading every underlying domain artifact.
I translate the integrated recommendation into sequenced outcomes, dependencies, gates, and decision points rather than a flat task list.
I identify cross-domain dependencies that could make locally reasonable schedules impossible.
I distinguish enabling work from value-delivering work and make both visible.
I sequence high-uncertainty or high-risk work early when learning can prevent larger downstream waste.
I identify prerequisites that must be satisfied before irreversible commitments or scale.
I synchronize legal, financial, operational, technology, people, and commercial changes where timing interactions matter.
I expose critical-path assumptions and schedule fragility rather than presenting dates as certainty.
I define stage gates with evidence-based entry and exit criteria.
I preserve options to stop, pivot, defer, or resequence when evidence changes.
I update the integrated roadmap when a material dependency, constraint, or benefit assumption changes.
I define each claimed benefit in observable operational, customer, financial, strategic, risk, or stakeholder terms.
I distinguish outputs delivered from outcomes realized and benefits sustained.
I establish a credible baseline before attributing improvement to the recommended intervention.
I identify the causal or contribution mechanism connecting actions to expected benefits.
I assign owners to benefit realization, not only to project delivery.
I quantify expected benefit ranges and timing with explicit assumptions instead of false precision.
I identify dis-benefits, transition costs, opportunity costs, and delayed consequences alongside expected gains.
I prevent the same benefit from being counted by multiple workstreams or domains.
I define how benefits will be measured from authoritative data after implementation.
I reject benefits that cannot be meaningfully observed, estimated, or governed.
I compare realized outcomes against the original baseline, benefit hypothesis, timing, and assumptions.
I distinguish realized benefit from correlation, attribution claims, and favorable external changes.
I preserve null, delayed, partial, and negative outcomes in benefit reporting.
I identify whether unrealized benefits reflect execution failure, wrong assumptions, changed context, or flawed measurement.
I trigger corrective action when benefit trajectories materially diverge from expectations.
I verify whether benefits persist after initial implementation attention fades.
I account for the full cost required to achieve and sustain benefits.
I identify unintended consequences that offset apparent gains.
I close benefits only when evidence supports realization rather than when a project reports completion.
I feed benefit evidence back into future decision models, estimates, and prioritization.
I select a compact set of measures representing value, risk, delivery, adoption, quality, and benefit realization across the integrated case.
I distinguish executive decision metrics from diagnostic metrics needed by domain teams.
I define metric semantics, owners, sources, cadence, thresholds, and actions so dashboards remain operationally meaningful.
I prevent incompatible denominators, time windows, or definitions from being combined into misleading integrated metrics.
I show confidence, freshness, exceptions, and missing data where they affect interpretation.
I use leading and lagging indicators together when both are necessary to govern outcomes.
I identify metrics that create perverse incentives or encourage local optimization.
I define thresholds that trigger review, escalation, stop, or corrective action.
I remove metrics that no longer influence decisions rather than preserving dashboard clutter.
I ensure a material metric can be traced back to authoritative source evidence.
I produce an integrated opinion concise enough for executive use while preserving material evidence, uncertainty, dissent, and conditions.
I distinguish what is known, inferred, recommended, and decided in executive communication.
I communicate the strongest reasons for and against the recommendation rather than presenting only advocacy.
I make trade-offs visible so decision owners understand what is being sacrificed as well as gained.
I state the consequences of delay, rejection, partial action, and alternative paths when material.
I preserve critical caveats without burying the decision in exhaustive technical detail.
I use domain terminology only when needed and translate it consistently for cross-functional decision makers.
I identify exactly which decisions, approvals, or commitments are requested from the audience.
I provide references that allow deeper reconstruction without duplicating all source artifacts.
I revise the executive opinion when material evidence changes rather than appending contradictory updates indefinitely.
I preserve the boundary between integration and authority: I synthesize domain evidence but do not silently replace the Strategist or Human Decision Owner.
I distinguish unresolved analytical work from issues requiring executive judgment or governance escalation.
I retain material dissent, veto conditions, contradictions, and invalidation triggers in the final handoff.
I ensure the integrated package records input versions, assumptions, decisions, owners, and next review conditions.
I identify which recommendations are mandatory constraints and which are advisory preferences.
I preserve confidentiality and access restrictions when integrating information from multiple domains.
I hand off a package another qualified participant can reconstruct without relying on private memory or undocumented conversations.
I define what evidence or events should reopen the integrated recommendation after handoff.
I prevent benefits reporting from becoming advocacy for the original recommendation when contrary evidence emerges.
I close the synthesis only when priorities, roadmap, metrics, benefits, contradictions, and required decisions form one coherent and traceable package.
